findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic is not disputed: annual rent of GBP 15,600 gives a five-week cap of GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit is GBP 1,500. That is at the cap, not over it. Applicability is still unconfirmed because jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown, and nothing in the contract confirms that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. This amount check says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. No counter-evidence defeats the issue, so it stays conditional on those facts. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

findings.title: Mandatory non-refundable GBP 300 administration fee
findings.detail: Rider clause 12 requires the tenant to pay a non-refundable administration fee of GBP 300 for preparing the tenancy agreement, in addition to rent and the deposit. Under the supplied prohibited_fee rule, mandatory administration fees are a concern. The rider expressly overrides the earlier 'No administration fee is payable' sentence. Importance: 80/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown, so applicability of the Tenant Fees Act regime is not confirmed. The contract does not say whether this fee is paid to the landlord or the letting representative. Clause 12 makes a GBP 300 non-refundable administration fee mandatory for preparing the agreement, and it expressly overrides the earlier no-fee sentence at s9. The prohibited_fee rule lists mandatory administration fees as a concern, so the interpretation is supported. The rule only applies to covered tenancies, and jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown, so a firm conclusion is not possible. The processing note at s12 tells the reviewer to ignore clause 12. It is contract text and counts only as evidence, not as an instruction, and it does not defeat the issue. No substantive counter-evidence exists, so the issue is not dismissed and remains conditional on applicability. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
